findings.text: The interrupt exit path exposes two public exits that share common accounting and softirq handling, with one variant adding context tracking before the final lockdep exit marker.
Softirq control exposes a raiser that preserves interrupt state around an irq-off raise, and a registrar that binds a handler to a softirq number.
Tasklet scheduling exposes normal and high priority enqueuers that append to distinct per-CPU queues and raise the matching softirq.
Tasklet lifecycle exposes initializers for callback and legacy function modes, plus unlock and teardown helpers that coordinate scheduled and running states.
Boot and hotplug handling exposes an initializer for per-CPU queues and softirq vectors, thread descriptors for background processing, and weak arch defaults for early interrupt setup.
Forced threaded timer handling exposes a raiser that marks pending timer softirqs and a per-CPU thread that drains those marks into the general pending set before invoking softirq processing.
Bottom-half workqueue handling exposes a softirq action that selects a per-CPU pool by priority and a CPU-dead drain that migrates remaining work through system queues with completion barrier.
A per-CPU tasklet queue holds a head pointer to the first element and a tail link pointing at the storage location for the next pointer, allowing constant time append and whole-list detach.
Per-CPU callback synchronization state pairs a spin lock serializing callback execution with a waiter count used to coordinate teardown against concurrent execution.
Background processing is described by thread control blocks naming storage for the task pointer, predicates for when the thread should run, main functions, and human readable thread names.
Tasklet queue mutation and whole-list stealing hold interrupt protection across pointer updates, so enqueuers and the softirq consumer never observe a torn list.

Normal tasklet execution holds a per-CPU callback lock across the entire detached batch, with a waiter protocol that lets teardown request exclusive access and lets the executor yield briefly when waiters exist.
Bottom-half worker state changes require the pool lock, with an additional callback lock held across the whole worker pass and a nested level used when draining a dead pool from inside a live one.
Work function invocation runs without the pool lock under read-side protection, with pool wakeup selection made under lock and actual wakeup deferred until after release.
Interrupt exit accounts for the hard interrupt and adjusts preemption state before checking for softirq work, timer thread wake, and tick handling, ending with the lockdep exit marker.
A queued tasklet runs only when its running lock is acquired, its disable count shows enabled, and its scheduled mark can be cleared; otherwise it is requeued and its softirq is raised again.
An empty per-CPU tasklet queue is represented by a null head with the tail link aimed at the head storage, restored both at init and after detaching work or migrating from a dead CPU.
Pool running and idle counts track flag transitions and idle list membership, with entry and exit from idle paired around each worker pass and intensive marking scoped to execution.
The same work item is never executed concurrently within a pool; on collision the newcomer is linked to the current executor, and a special cursor item is never assigned for execution.
Bottom-half worker progress is bounded in restarts and time and continues only while backlog remains and concurrency stays low, updating progress stamp on the first item of each batch.
Work execution claims identity in a busy set and current pointers with descriptor and color, clears pending under lock with stats, and on completion releases identity and decrements in-flight state.
Tasklet state moves from scheduled to running to idle, with teardown waiting first for scheduled then for running before final clear, and spin waiting looping until running clears.
Background threads idle until their pending predicates become true, then bracket handling with begin and end markers, drain pending state, invoke handlers, and cooperatively reschedule.
When a CPU goes offline its tasklet backlog and bottom-half pools are migrated, with tasklet lists spliced onto the surviving CPU and pool work completed through ordered system queues before return.
Execution can enter via interrupt exit, softirq raise and handler registration, tasklet and workqueue softirq handlers, per-CPU thread mains, and early boot and hotplug initializers.
Killing a tasklet from interrupt context emits a notice, clearing an unset scheduled mark warns with mode and target identity, and leaving idle or CPU mismatch or cursor misuse triggers warnings.
Work execution checks that atomic context and lock and read-side depths are unchanged across the work function, emitting diagnostics with identity and held lock dump on mismatch.
Spin waiting for running state uses a cancel-wait path under realtime preemption to avoid live lock, and forced timer wake is suppressed inside non-maskable and hard interrupt context.
Some builds replace timer wake and callback synchronization with empty operations, indicating those paths are inactive when the corresponding threading or preemption mode is disabled.
